newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA SHARES END LOWER, REVERSE EARLY GAINS.
newsitem.headline: MANILA SHARES END LOWER, REVERSE EARLY GAINS.

text.p: Philippine shares settled lower on Wednesday amid light trade, failing to sustain the early climb as investors cashed in short-term profits, brokers said.
"The selling momentum has slowed down although people are watching where the market is headed before aggressively putting in their money," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.
The main index shed 8.32 points, closing at 2,527.08. It was in positive territory until midtrade, reaching an intra-day high of 2,553.09 points.

"Most of the funds are transferring to the fixed income instruments. We do not see much interest in the market due to the forex uncertainty and the lingering high interest rates," said Antonio Legarda, sales manager at DBP-Daiwa Securities.
Turnover was modest at 1.69 billion pesos, lower than the previous day's close of 2.23 billion.
In the broad market, decliners trampled gainers, 75 to 35.
"Buyers are coming in in trickles ... We should still see things on the downside," said Juanis Barredo, analyst at Citisecurities Inc.
Of the blue chips, only Ayala Land Inc and Philipine Long Distance Telephone Co were active gainers.

"There's not much buying incentive. To take the market back up, investors should be assured first that the currency assault has died down," said Helen Alvarez, research director at All Asia Securities.
Traders expect the market to test the support of 2,500 in the coming days.
